label: models/fw_walllamp.mdl: a caged wall lamp with a sodium-orange glass

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_rpgammo.mdl, models/w_chainammo.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, D, D where the asset was A, B, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a caged wall lamp with a sodium-orange glass), every view reads right. The front shows a vertical steel backplate with a round orange glass inside a black wire cage. The side and top views show the cage standing out from the plate on a short bracket. The back view shows a plain plate with a small square mount stub. Nothing sticks out or is missing in any of the ten views.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the lamp, so there is no size to be within 15% of. The measured 20.5 x 16 x 22 units is a plausible size for a wall lamp, and nothing in the pictures is clearly off in scale against the lineup.

M3.reason: The parts the brief asks for are all there: the wall plate (front and back views), the cage of black wire bars (front, left, top and below views), the orange glass inside it (front view and the oblique views), and the bracket joining plate and cage (left and top views). The back view's small square mount stub is also present. The brief names no other small parts (no rivets, handles or claws), so none is missing.

M4.reason: The plate is grey steel, the cage black wire and the glass sodium orange, which matches the brief's palette and its sodium-orange glass. The glass shows a bright core fading to deeper orange at the edges, as a lit sodium glass would. No region is a colour the brief does not ask for.

M5.reason: The plate carries horizontal grain and lighter bevelled edges, and the glass has fine faceted banding and a lit core, so the surface reads as worn steel and a glowing lamp. The brief asks for nothing more specific than the glow and the wear, and both are present at a similar sharpness across the views.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric's rule that M6 is measured apart by the line-up. In the line-up test the asset was picked as the non-Valve item in one of four readings (judges picked C, D, D, D where the asset was A, B, D, C), so it passed for one of the game's on the test as run.

M7.reason: The front is the cage side, with the orange glass and cage facing the viewer and the plate behind. The lamp stands upright, with its plate vertical as a wall mount is. The model's origin does not appear in any picture, so the placement on the origin is not checked beyond that.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 88 triangles it is well within twice the median (99) and under the third quartile (156) of Half-Life's own props of its kind, so the triangle count passes. No open or inside-out faces show from any view. The cage is joined to the plate by the bracket in the left, top and below views, so nothing floats.
